html:
The Barasana are an Eastern Tukanoan people of the Pirá-Paraná River in the Vaupés region of southeast Colombia. They live in large communal longhouses, called malocas, and grow bitter manioc, fish and hunt.

In the Vaupés, people must marry someone who speaks a different language, so most households use several languages. The Barasana marry with the Tatuyo, Karapana and Makuna, among others. Their ceremonies with sacred flutes, linked to the ancestral anaconda, were studied closely by the anthropologists Stephen and Christine Hugh-Jones in the 1960s and 1970s. The rubber boom and missionaries reached the area from the late 1800s.
